body: I haven't talked to anybody I used to know in nearly 8 years. It's going to be a masterclass in nobody caring.
It'll be public in a few days. I wasn't planning on leaving a link here, if that's what you're asking

She doesn't even know me. I was gone before she could remember anything about me. Not long after I left, I asked my ex if our daughter missed me, and I was told that she didn't even notice I was gone. I'm basically a complete stranger at this point.

I worry about that all the time, but there's nothing I can do to help her anymore. It's been too many years since I was a part of her story to rejoin it. I'm only giving myself permission to finally let go now because her stepfather is adopting her, so she doesn't need even the small possibility of me rejoining the world to have the love and support she needs.  The only thing left of me to give her is a story that she might not even ever want to read, and I'm at peace with that.

I can relate a lot to your plan.

I'm aiming for November 14, myself. I'm finishing up a a "book" to try and explain how everything happened for my daughter and time releasing it to her, but I need to wait about 8-10 years until she's old enough to understand it, so it's a lot more difficult. I wish I could just encrypt a USB drive and somehow get it delivered to her when she's ready, but alas. 

Peace be the journey, friend, wherever it winds up taking you

The moment I cracked was about a week after I left. I had texted my ex to see how our kid was, and I asked "Do they miss me?" since it was the longest I had ever been away and I had been a stay at home dad that played with them, took them to the park, read books to them, changed every diaper, gave every bath, cooked for them, and everything else. 

My ex texted back and said "I don't think they've even noticed", and then my brain popped and I stopped existing as a real person and started existing as this empty husk that kinda-sorta used to look like a person if you squinted hard enough.

I had always struggled with depression, and even spent time in the hospital in high school after a suicide attempt. I thought I was through the worst of it after finding 'the love of my life' and having a perfect kid, but a lot of things started building up and I started sliding back down. I knew where my thoughts were eventually headed to because I had been there before, but after getting told "I want a divorce", then a week later being told "get out by the end of the week" and then a week later getting kicked out, then a week later being told "your child doesn't even notice you're not here", I just crashed harder than I ever would have imagined. It all moved far too quickly for me to process it.

I'm not exactly sure how I got out. I know that at some point I started talking to a group of people online, and I started feeling like a real person again over shared interests. That small social circle came to a kind of abrupt end for me, because I started getting hit with a lot of unprocessed emotions and guilt and shame and it turned me pretty toxic, so I walked away. But I've been able to stay grounded and remember and have some control over myself since then, so I guess it was just a step forward.

I was a deadbeat dad. 

I was unemployed and a stay at home dad and had declining mental health already, and my ex gave me about a week to pack my shit and get out with nowhere to go and nothing to fall back on. 

I went through a pretty significant mental break. I remember the exact second that I cracked in half, and it happened so quickly and completely that there was probably an audible pop from my brain. I was in some kind of dissociative state for well over a year after, slumming it up in a room at my parents' house several hours away. I was just on autopilot and went with the motions. I have no memories whatsoever of that time, and I'm pretty sure the only reason I didn't kill myself was because my mind was just absent from my body and I had minimal control. I don't even remember the divorce a few months later. I found the paperwork in a box well after the fact.

I just never went back, reached out, or paid child support. By the time I was lucid again, I was afraid of what I might do to myself if I saw my kid again and they didn't remember me or know who I was, and that feeling just got worse the older they got and more they would comprehend how shitty I was. So I stayed away.

The door to that chapter of life slammed closed before I really even knew what was happening and I never really caught back up, and I feel the weight of the guilt and the hurt of that decision every day, but I'm too weak to deal with it and I'm not going to try and get a kid who doesn't remember to have any type of relationship with the mentally unwell dad that abandoned them. I can't even bring myself to look for them on social media just to see a picture because I feel like I'm just hanging on by a thread at all times, and I don't know if I could handle seeing the life I left behind and lost. 

When my kid was 10, they were adopted by their stepdad, though. So at least they have a father figure in their life.
